items.title: Erecting Cathedrals
items.summary: In sweat and blood they birthed the stones. Their backs bent in…
items.content_html:
In sweat and blood they birthed the stones.
Their backs bent in a dimly lit choreography,  
they strained to hoist the ashlars into place.
Thirty-six years in a most sacred guild,
they each apprenticed the other.
 
Their aging bodies lust for sleep,
but it runs from them into the cold night.
Lying there, limbs entwined for warmth,
their calloused fingers touch scars,
which mark passing time on their rounding frames.
 
They remember the works of their labors.
The six structures on which they’ve toiled.
Their six children raised with hope.
The six cathedrals in whom they pray,
both their memories and Christ will dwell.

items.title: Maternal Silence
items.summary: She was a young woman, from a world of chaos. But She…
items.content_html:
She was a young woman,
from a world of
chaos.
 
But She tried to hide
that chaos behind her
smile.
 
At first she would hear
me crying in the
crib.
 
But by the time I talked,
her world was
silent.
 
She would watch my lips
while I said my
prayers.
 
But sometimes I would peek
at her with one
eye.
 
Records played in her head,
which only she could
hear.
 
But we would often
dance to their
beat.
 
She taught me old lyrics,
which we sang
off-key.
 
But those melodies
are still my
favorite.

items.title: Our Funeral
items.summary: We bury today our Alleluia. It is not dead, but on deposit,…
items.content_html:
We bury today our Alleluia.
It is not dead,
but on deposit,
as our brother,
who sleeps.

But we who amble on,
don this burlap,
and turn our,
face to ash,
in penance.


This Lent more somber,
as bombs fall,
as children flee,
while we wait,
His return.

items.content_html:

items.title: My Deaf Mom
items.summary: She lived her life with an immature desire. Dancing and singing, her…
items.content_html:
She lived her life with an immature desire.
Dancing and singing, her face lit a room.
But like a firecracker before the boom,
many often held their breath while by her.
 
I remember once, while near that line of fire,
I blushed, a boy of five, from her strong fume.
Her lips spewing forth in an obscene plume,
while she alone would not hear the deafening ire.
 
Then I’d relay the circumspect reply,
from a confused face speaking through her child,
as my mother lit a fresh cigarette.
 
Rewinding the tape with her careful eye,
she watched me imitate the words which riled,
never showing me a small sign of regret.

items.title: Bread
items.summary: I smell the bread baking and I’m reminded of your soft hands…
items.content_html:
I smell the bread baking
and I’m reminded of your soft hands
touching that fleshy dough.
You make me hungry.
 
As steam and hot scent
escape from the oven door,
I see our reflection in the glass.
My face is covered in sweat.
 
Though you give me a generous slice,
hot with salted butter;
even while the taste still lingers,
I want more.

items.title: Autumn
items.summary: I looked out for you, but frost covered my window. Summer, did…
items.content_html:
I looked out for you,
but frost covered my window.
Summer, did you leave?

items.summary: Lipstick red, your massive hips bulge above supple feet, as my finger…
items.content_html:
Lipstick red,
your massive hips
bulge above supple feet,
as my finger gently traces
their obscene curve.
Anticipating that
provocative,
pulsing,
power,
perched
between your thick thighs,
I take my seat
and eagerly
turn the key.

items.title: Liquor
items.summary: The poetic word is potent. Like one hundred and seven proof bourbon,…
items.content_html:
The poetic word is potent.
Like one hundred and seven proof
bourbon,
it makes me drunk.

Plenty of pages of prose
are distilled in
a single
verse.

It is irresistible as
I swirl it in my mouth.
Sniff it.
Taste it.

I breathe it in.

I hold it up to the light
to peer into its soul.

With voracious appetite,
I invert its glass until

the

last

drip

slides
so
slowly

onto my 
silver
tongue.

items.title: Paper Airplane
items.summary: If you chance find this poem, please do not attempt reply. Just…
items.content_html:
If you chance find this poem,
please do not attempt reply.
Just fold it back into its shape
and toss it toward the sky.
 
I launched it late last night,
out the window in my room,
a sort of self-made prison space
above my future tomb.
 
Thirty years I’ve toiled
on this edifice of gold.
Performing tasks I scarce enjoy,
a slab of me I sold.
 
A dream to be a poet
is at my very core.
Perhaps, some day, I’ll muster strength
and become what I adore.
 
This airplane sent aloft,
out on the chill night air,
it is a verse from Morpheus,
a hope, a dream, my prayer.
